# Ecclesiastes Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 412r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/ECC_012_page_001.jpg

---

**12:1** And-remember [u-zekhor] your-Creator [bore'ekha] in-the-days of-your-youth [bechurotekha], before [ad asher] the-evil [ha-ra'ah] days [yemei] come [yavo'u], and-the-years [shanot] arrive [higgiu] of-which you-will-say, "I-have-no [ein li] pleasure [chefets] in-them."

**12:7** And-the-dust [ha-afar] returns [yashuv] to the-earth [al-ha-arets] as-it-was [she-hayah], and-the-spirit [veha-ruach] returns to the-God [ha-elohim] who gave-it [netatnah].

**12:8** Vapor of-vapors [havel havalim], says Qohelet; the-all [ha-kol] [is] vapor.

**12:13** The-end [sof] of-the-matter [davar]; the-all [ha-kol] has-been-heard [nishma]: Fear [yera] the-God [ha-elohim] and-keep [shemor] his-commandments [mitsvotav]; for this [is] the-whole [kol] of-man [ha-adam].

**12:14** For every deed [ma'aseh] the-God will-bring [yavi] into-judgment [be-mishpat], over [al] every hidden-thing [ne'lam], whether good [tov] or [im] evil [ra].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1-7 — The aging allegory:** Physical decline in coded imagery: "keepers of the house tremble" (arms shake), "grinders cease" (teeth lost), "those looking through windows grow dim" (eyes fail), "the silver cord is snapped" (death).

**v.13-14 — The epilogue:** Written in third person about Qohelet. Its function — framing radical questioning within conventional piety ("fear God and keep his commandments") — may have facilitated the book's acceptance into the canon.

*— EMET*
